question: What is the main feature of a unit dispensing system?

options.A: Medications are supplied in ready-to-administer individual doses
options.B: Nurses store large bulk supplies of drugs directly on the ward
options.C: Doctors dispense medications straight from the clinic consultation room
options.D: Patients purchase all their prescribed drugs from outside pharmacies

explanation: The core design of this system is to package drugs individually so they are ready for a specific patient at a specific time. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h1)

question: How does the unit dose system differ from traditional ward stock methods?

options.A: Nurses take over full responsibility for compounding intravenous fluids
options.B: Preparation shifts from busy clinical wards to the central pharmacy
options.C: Patients completely manage their own drug schedules without supervision
options.D: Hospital pharmacists no longer verify doctor prescriptions before supply

explanation: Moving the drug preparation task away from the noisy ward into the pharmacy reduces interruptions and lowers the risk of mistakes. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h1)

question: What was a major issue with patients bringing bulk drug supplies to Nigerian hospital wards?

options.B: Poor storage conditions and lost medications
options.D: Immediate electronic tracking of every pill

explanation: Bulk drugs kept in ward lockers were frequently misplaced, stolen, or exposed to heat and moisture, which ruined their potency. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h2)

question: How does unit dispensing improve financial transparency for patients?

options.A: Medication prices are standardized across all states
options.B: Hospital care becomes completely free of charge
options.C: Invoices are calculated based on hospital stay duration
options.D: Patients pay only for the exact doses administered

explanation: Instead of buying an entire pack of fifty tablets when only five are needed, the patient only pays for those five doses. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a unit dose cart on a hospital ward?

options.A: Serving as an emergency resuscitation trolley for cardiac arrest
options.B: Holding individual patient medication drawers for safe rounds
options.C: Transporting large bulk fluid bags from the main central store
options.D: Storing personal medical files and patient charts securely

explanation: The unit dose cart contains separate locked or labeled sections for each patient so the nurse can administer drugs safely bed-to-bed. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is the patient medication profile essential in a unit dose setup?

options.A: It ensures that hospital billing departments track patient food preferences
options.B: It allows nurses to diagnose minor illnesses without consulting doctors
options.C: It replaces the need for any verbal or written communication on the ward
options.D: It gives pharmacists a clear, real-time record to check before supplying doses

explanation: The pharmacist relies on this active profile to verify dosages and catch potential drug interactions before packaging the individual doses. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h3)

question: What step immediately follows the physician writing a prescription in the unit dispensing workflow?

options.A: The pharmacist reviews and verifies the order
options.B: The ward cleaner organizes the medication cart
options.C: The nurse administers the drug immediately
options.D: The patient pays the hospital cashier

explanation: Before any medication is picked or packaged, the pharmacist must check the prescription for safety and correct dosing. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing to give a 10:00 AM medication dose using the unit dispensing cart. When is the best time to document that the drug was given?

options.A: Whenever the nurse remembers during the afternoon visiting hours
options.B: Before leaving the central pharmacy room with the mobile drug cart
options.C: Immediately after the patient swallows the medication at the bedside
options.D: At the end of the shift when all patient charts are gathered together

explanation: Documentation must happen right after administration to prevent accidental double-dosing or missed records. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main responsibility of the nurse at the bedside during unit dispensing?

options.A: Checking the chemical purity of drugs inside the pharmacy lab
options.B: Packaging the individual pills into small plastic wrappers
options.C: Performing final safety checks and administering the drug
options.D: Calculating the bulk wholesale cost of each medication dose

explanation: The nurse is the last person to see the patient before ingestion, making bedside verification essential to catch any lingering errors. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which professional group acts as the primary defense against prescribing and dosage errors before drugs reach the ward?
explanation: Pharmacists review the initial orders and verify clinical safety before preparing the individual doses for distribution. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why does the unit dose system lead to fewer medication errors on the wards?

options.A: Nurses no longer need to check patient wristbands before giving drugs
options.B: Clear labeling and professional pharmacy preparation reduce guesswork
options.C: Doctors stop changing medication orders once the patient is admitted
options.D: Patients completely take over the responsibility of drug management

explanation: Pre-packaged, individually labeled doses remove the need for nurses to measure or split pills under high-pressure ward conditions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does unit dispensing help reduce financial waste in hospitals?

options.A: By tracking consumption accurately and allowing return of unsealed doses
options.B: By forcing patients to buy their medications from private vendors outside
options.C: By charging patients high penalty fees for missed medication doses
options.D: By eliminating the need for any professional pharmacy staff on duty

explanation: Precise tracking prevents excess purchasing, and sealed returned medications can be safely reissued to other patients. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is a major manpower challenge when setting up unit dispensing in resource-limited hospitals?

options.A: Excessive numbers of idle staff wandering around the wards
options.B: Shortage of registered pharmacists and trained technicians
options.C: Too many foreign consultants interfering with local protocols
options.D: Unwillingness of nursing staff to work morning shifts

explanation: A lack of adequate professional staff creates bottlenecks in reviewing prescriptions and preparing individual doses on time. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why do hospitals in resource-limited settings often start unit dispensing in high-risk units first?

options.A: To maximize safety impact where vulnerable patients need it most
options.B: To comply with international rules regarding surgical theatres only
options.C: To hide implementation failures from hospital management boards
options.D: To test equipment durability without involving any professional staff

explanation: Starting in units like intensive care or pediatrics targets areas where medication mistakes can cause the most severe harm. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is a key policy step needed to improve medication dispensing systems nationally?

options.A: Making all prescription drugs completely free for every citizen
options.B: Transferring all nursing duties to the central pharmacy department
options.C: Banning the use of mobile carts in all public healthcare facilities
options.D: Including unit dose standards in hospital accreditation requirements

explanation: Enforcing standards through official accreditation ensures hospitals allocate necessary resources to maintain safe dispensing practices. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which technology helps link patient prescriptions directly with pharmacy dispensing software?

options.A: Manual paper ledgers stored in wooden cabinets
options.B: Electronic health records and barcoding systems
options.C: Standard telephone landlines on the ward
options.D: Traditional wall clocks placed in the hallway

explanation: Digital records and barcode scanners speed up order transmission and reduce transcription mistakes between departments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h8)
